CONTEXT.content: Dependencies fail. Graceful degradation keeps core functionality working when non-critical services are down.
CONTEXT.analogy: Airplane loses entertainment system — flight continues. Loses engine — different story.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Users prefer slow partial service over total outage.
hints: What's critical vs nice-to-have in your app?

DECIDE.optionA: Fail fast: return errors immediately when dependencies are unhealthy.
DECIDE.optionB: Degrade gracefully: serve cached/stale data or skip optional features.

tradeoffs.A: Honest errors; worse UX during partial outages.
tradeoffs.B: Better UX; risk of serving stale or inconsistent data.

hints: When is stale data worse than an error?

BUILD.goal: Add a fallback when a non-critical dependency fails (e.g., analytics, recommendations). Core path still works.

tracks.node: Try/catch with timeout; return default when dependency times out.

acceptance: Core feature works when dependency is down
Response indicates degraded state if appropriate
hints: Set timeouts on every outbound call.

criteria: Kill dependency — core path still returns 200
hints: Test with dependency slow, not just down.

BREAK.scenario: Fallback cache serves user data from another user's session.
BREAK.symptoms: Privacy incident. Fallback key was too generic.

FIX.goal: Fix cache key scoping. Add circuit breaker to stop hammering failed dependency.
hints: Never share fallback data across tenants.

decisionCallbacks.A: Fail fast avoided stale data bugs but users saw more errors during outages.
decisionCallbacks.B: Degradation improved UX until cache scoping caused a privacy issue — scope matters.
